channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: A ambição de Eduardo Cunha se for eleito para a Câmara
item.description: Eduardo Cunha, a controversial figure in Brazilian politics, seeks not only re-election to the Chamber of Deputies in 2026 but also aims to return to the presidency of the House. His ambition extends beyond a simple term, indicating a long-term strategy to regain political influence following his past controversies and convictions.

item.title: TSE define regras para alistamento eleitoral e cadastro biométrico
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) established, through Resolution No. 23.759/2026, the rules for voter registration and biometric registration ahead of the 2026 elections. Voter registration is mandatory for literate Brazilians aged 18 to 70 and optional for 16-17-year-olds, those over 70, and illiterate citizens, with a final registration deadline of May 6, 2026. The process requires documents such as ID, proof of residence, and military service compliance (when applicable), and is guaranteed to Brazilians aged 16 or older and Portuguese citizens who have acquired political rights in Brazil.

item.title: À moda Trump, voluntários da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro trabalham em missão específica
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign has around 100 volunteers dedicated to drafting legislative proposals to be presented to Congress on the first day of government, if elected. The initiative, modeled after strategies like Trump's, aims to prepare an immediate governing agenda. Full access to the article requires a subscriber login.

item.title: Memes ligam suspensão de detergente Ypê ao governo Lula
item.description: Right-wing internet users linked the Anvisa's temporary suspension of certain Ypê detergent batches over microbiological contamination risks to an alleged political persecution by the Lula government, despite the measure being lifted after the manufacturer's appeal. The memes, often baseless, leveraged donations from the Beira family to Bolsonaro's 2022 campaign to imply political motives behind the health agency's action.

item.title: André Mendonça, Ciro e o fim da fábula da perseguição de Moraes
item.description: The authorization of the operation against Ciro Nogueira by Minister André Mendonça, appointed by Bolsonaro, dismantles the right-wing narrative of political persecution at the STF, showing the investigation originated from a Bolsonaro ally. Ciro Nogueira, who now cries 'scheduled timing,' overlooks that his rapporteur is a minister he himself supported during the Senate hearing. The case reveals that no politician is above the law, even within the Bolsonarist base.

item.title: Crítica ao STF mobiliza estratégia de campanha dos presidenciáveis da direita
item.description: Right-wing presidential pre-candidates, particularly Flávio Bolsonaro, are intensifying criticism of the STF as a campaign strategy, proposing reforms to limit its powers and increase accountability of justices amid institutional distrust and polarization. The narrative resonates strongly with right-wing voters, where up to 90% believe the Court holds excessive power and acts in favor of the Lula government, according to a Genial/Quaest survey. Other pre-candidates like Romeu Zema and Aldo Rebelo also advocate structural changes to the Court, making the judiciary a central theme to differentiate opposition candidacies.

item.title: Nem o PL aposta na permanência de Cláudio Castro na corrida ao Senado
item.description: No one in Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign or the PL's high command believes Cláudio Castro will remain a pre-candidate for the Senate in Rio de Janeiro for much longer. The exclusive subscriber-only report suggests that backing for his Senate bid is seen as weak or temporary.

item.title: Lula falou bem mais do que Trump em reunião
item.description: In a three-hour meeting between Lula and Donald Trump, the two presidents spoke for 80% of the time, with the Brazilian president speaking more than the American, according to a participant. The full article is available only to subscribers.

item.title: Caiado dispara contra STF após suspensão da Dosimetria: “Deplorável”
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD-GO) called the Supreme Court's suspension of the Dosimetria Law 'deplorable,' arguing it exacerbates political polarization and distracts from national priorities. He criticized the judiciary's interference in congressional affairs and urged an end to the conflict between the STF and Congress, advocating for institutional balance.

item.title: Como o PT explora a operação da PF contra Ciro Nogueira, ex-ministro de Bolsonaro
item.description: The Federal Police conducted an operation against Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) over allegations of receiving R$300,000 monthly from banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master in exchange for a PEC amendment to increase the FGTS guarantee fund. The Lula government’s base is using the case to attack the opposition, while Flávio Bolsonaro’s group seeks to tie the scandal to the STF and the PT. The amendment failed and Banco Master was liquidated in November 2025.

item.title: Últimas pesquisas eleitorais 2026: Quem está à frente na disputa para presidente?
item.description: Latest 2026 election polls show Lula (PT) leading the first round with 39% voting intention, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 36% and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) at 5%. In the Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro runoff scenario, the senator leads with 46% against 44% for the incumbent president. Other candidates such as Romeu Zema, Ciro Gomes, and Renan Santos are competing for third place.

item.title: O principal empecilho para um acordão entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Moraes
item.description: Allies of Lula's government suspect a possible 'big deal' between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and Minister Alexandre de Moraes to overturn vetoes on the Dosimetry Bill and benefit Jair Bolsonaro, but the main obstacle is the bolsonarists' historical tendency to break agreements, as noted by Moraes' allies and Bolsonaro family sources.

item.title: “Moraes ultrapassa os limites da relação institucional”, diz Caiado
item.description: Former governor Ronaldo Caiado criticized a decision by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes to suspend the Dosimetry Law, calling it an attack on democracy and the separation of powers.

item.title: A retaliação de Lula contra Davi Alcolumbre
item.description: Lula decided to maintain his alliance with Davi Alcolumbre despite the Senate president's efforts to block the nomination of Jorge Messias to the Supreme Court. The president intends to send a political signal to Alcolumbre, expressing dissatisfaction without formally breaking ties. The exclusive subscriber-only article details the institutional tensions behind the scenes.

item.title: Campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro se prepara para explorar passado lulista de Ciro Nogueira
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is distancing himself from Ciro Nogueira following a Federal Police operation investigating the former minister over alleged ties to Daniel Vorcaro. Despite previously praising Nogueira as having 'all the credentials' to be his running mate, Bolsonaro now seeks to dissociate his image from the ally amid new allegations. The move unfolds amid the evolving political landscape ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Minerais críticos expõem gargalo fundiário e desafio regulatório
item.description: The debate on critical minerals in Brazil, driven by the approval of a bill in Congress and the meeting between Lula and Trump, exposed weaknesses in territorial governance despite the country's vast reserves. Experts argue the issue is not a lack of legislation but the failure to integrate mineral titles, environmental licensing, land tenure regularity, and protected areas, leading to procedural insecurity and overlapping records. Advancing territorial intelligence, cadastral integration, and institutional coordination is essential to prevent conflicts and ensure economic sovereignty.

item.title: Alcolumbre abre caminho para Pacheco assumir vaga no TCU
item.description: Davi Alcolumbre failed to secure Rodrigo Pacheco as an STF minister but is now leading an effort to place Pacheco — whom Lula wanted as his Minas Gerais gubernatorial candidate — into a seat at the TCU. The move reflects behind-the-scenes congressional maneuvering to balance power among branches. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Tão perto, tão longe: Planalto e Congresso têm maior afastamento em 35 anos
item.description: In two days, the Lula government suffered significant defeats in Congress: the Senate vetoed the president's STF nomination, and the following day overturned his vetoes on the Dosimetry Bill, which benefits those convicted of the January 8 attacks and former President Jair Bolsonaro. This marks the greatest distance between the Planalto and Congress in 35 years.

item.title: A suposta ou real ignorância de Flávio Bolsonaro e Ronaldo Caiado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former governor Ronaldo Caiado criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes’ decision to suspend the Dosimetry Law, claiming it undermines democracy and constitutes harmful judicial activism. The article suggests their criticism is tactical, aiming to mislead voters and exploit far-right narratives about January 8, while disregarding the legal context: the suspension was a monocratic cautionary measure due to new ADIs filed by ABI and PSOL/Rede, not a final ruling on the law’s merit.

item.title: Indefinição do PT em Minas Gerais pode atrapalhar raro nome em ascensão no partido
item.description: The PT's indecision over its electoral slate in Minas Gerais may undermine the Senate pre-candidacy of former Contagem mayor Marília Campos, who would be tasked with organizing Lula’s campaign in the state. Party members are considering launching a ticket without a gubernatorial candidate, focusing only on Senate and congressional seats, which would place the burden of mobilizing voters on Marília. Despite her strong popularity — she was Brazil’s most-voted mayor in 2024 and leads in Senate polls — the lack of alliance definition and Lula’s 54% rejection rate in Minas create a difficult environment for her rise.

item.title: "Guerra" entre governo e Alcolumbre pode empacar regulamentação da IA
item.description: Aguinaldo Ribeiro, the rapporteur of the AI regulation bill in the Chamber of Deputies, warned that the ongoing conflict between the Lula government and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre could delay or distort the proposal. He advocates for postponing the vote until the government and Alcolumbre reach an agreement, as the bill—originally from the Senate—must be approved by senators with the Chamber’s amendments and government consensus.

item.title: Urna eletrônica faz 30 anos: ‘ninjas’ da tecnologia ajudaram a criar em São José máquina que transformou as eleições no Brasil; veja história
item.description: Brazil's electronic voting machine turns 30 in 2026, originating from a TSE initiative in 1995 with technological foundation provided by engineers from Inpe and CTA in São José dos Campos, nicknamed 'ninjas'. The project began with a conversation between then-minister Carlos Velloso and technician Paulo Camarão during a tennis match in December 1994, leading to the formation of committees that delivered the first electronic urns in May 1996.

item.title: A reviravolta total nas redes sociais sobre o encontro de Lula com Donald Trump
item.description: The meeting between Lula and Donald Trump at the White House sparked significant social media activity. Prior to the encounter, seven of the ten most engaged Instagram posts predicted a negative outcome for the Brazilian president. After the discussion, the narrative reversed, with only one critical post among the top ten interactions, indicating a notable shift in public perception.

item.title: Presidência do Senado: eleição será só em 2027, mas já movimenta articulações em Brasília; saiba por quê
item.description: The election for the presidency of the Federal Senate will take place only on February 1, 2027, but political maneuvers in Brasília have already begun. Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil‑AP), the current Senate president elected in 2025, is seeking re-election and has built a broad coalition spanning the Lula government, the Centrão, and opposition parties, including the PT and PL. His role is pivotal: he presides over Congress, oversees the confirmation of STF and regulatory agency nominees, and can initiate impeachment proceedings against Supreme Court justices, as demonstrated by the historic rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination in April 2024.

item.title: Partidos fecham ano eleitoral com dívida mesmo com fundão bilionário
item.description: Despite access to nearly R$5 billion from the Electoral Fund, political parties closed 2024 with deficits, spending more than they raised. The PL led the imbalance in 2022 with a R$78.7 million deficit, followed by PSDB and PT, which also recorded negative balances in election years. The strategy of accumulating resources in non-election years to spend beyond the fund’s allocation is common, though under review by the TSE.

item.title: Um em cada cinco brasileiros já foi alvo de tentativa de compra de voto
item.description: An Ipsos-Ipec survey shows that 22% of Brazilians have received offers to sell their vote, with municipal positions — particularly city councilors (59%) and mayors (43%) — being the most common sources of coercion. Most respondents do not feel safe reporting the crime, and many fail to recognize non-monetary forms of vote-buying, such as medical consultations or parties, viewing them merely as 'favors'. The Northeast region reports the highest incidence at 32%, while 39% believe such practices occur 'always' in their area.

item.title: Flávio, Caiado e Zema batem ponto em eventos do agro e disputam palanque em feiras e rodeios, antes palco único de Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, Ronaldo Caiado, and Romeu Zema are competing for the support of the agribusiness electorate at events such as the rodeos in Barretos, Jaguariúna, and Americana—spaces once dominated exclusively by Jair Bolsonaro. The 2026 agro fair and rodeo season has become a new political stage for right-wing presidential pre-candidates seeking to strengthen their base in this influential sector.

item.title: O voto nos estados: em eleição sob a sombra do Master, PT busca sexto mandato na Bahia em disputa com o carlismo
item.description: In Bahia, PT governor Jerônimo Rodrigues seeks re-election against ACM Neto (União Brasil), former mayor of Salvador and representative of the carlist political machine, in a rematch of the 2022 race marked by a technical tie in polls and mutual efforts to keep the Banco Master scandal out of the campaign. Despite the Carlists’ four-decade historical dominance, the PT has controlled the state since 2007, with Jerônimo winning in 2022 by a narrow margin (52.78% to 47.22%). The April Genial/Quaest poll shows ACM Neto at 41% and Jerônimo at 38% in a simulated runoff, with 47% of voters saying they could change their choice.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro, el hijo con la misión de derrotar a Lula y conquistar el poder en Brasil
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign event in Florianópolis, initially scheduled for 2:22 PM as a nod to the number 22 used by Bolsonaros on electronic ballots, started an hour late due to rain. Held in Santa Catarina—a right-wing stronghold—the event featured street vendors selling Flávio Bolsonaro 2026 merchandise. The article outlines the Bolsonaro clan’s strategy to use the city as a political showcase ahead of the 2026 elections, aiming to defeat Lula and seize national power.

item.title: Trama golpista: como ficam as reduções de pena; entenda decisão de Moraes que suspendeu aplicação da Lei da Dosimetria
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended the application of the Dosimetry Law until the full court rules on its constitutionality, affecting sentence reduction requests from those convicted in the January 8 attacks, including former President Jair Bolsonaro. The decision is based on pending direct actions challenging the law and aims to ensure legal certainty until the STF's final ruling.

item.title: Kassio tenta blindagem no TSE contra questionamento às urnas e mira se diferenciar de Moraes
item.description: The new president of the TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, is preparing to face challenges to the security and reliability of electronic voting machines following the disinformation that marked the 2022 elections. His leadership aims to shield the tribunal from attacks on electoral integrity while seeking to differentiate himself from the approach of Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Kassio assumirá presidência do TSE para comandar eleições de 2026; veja histórico da corte
item.description: Kassio Nunes Marques will assume the presidency of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on September 12, 2026, following a symbolic vote in April, in accordance with the seniority-based rotation among STF justices. He will oversee the 2026 general elections, with André Mendonça serving as vice-president of the court.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro lança jingle de campanha feito por IA: “Entrar com o pé direito”
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro launched an AI-generated campaign jingle with the slogan 'enter on the right foot', aiming to mobilize supporters to 'straighten out Brazil'. The song, accompanied by an AI-generated video, was released at an event in Santa Catarina and references the 2023 Havaianas ad, which right-wing supporters interpreted as a political indirect message. The initiative reinforces the campaign identity of Flávio, Carlos Bolsonaro, and Carol De Toni for the Senate, emphasizing hope, unity, and national reconstruction.

item.title: Flávio lança novo jingle: “Com o pé direito, o Brasil tem futuro”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) launched his presidential pre-campaign jingle, 'With the right foot, Brazil has a future', at a PL event in Florianópolis, referencing a 2025 controversy with Havaianas over the phrase 'right foot'. The event also formalized the Senate pre-candidacies of Carlos Bolsonaro and federal deputy Carol De Toni (PL-SC), as well as Governor Jorginho Mello’s (PL-SC) re-election bid. National and state PL leaders attended.

item.title: Lula exalta “frango nordestino” ao receber aves na Granja do Torto
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva praised a genuinely Brazilian chicken breed, the 'northeastern chicken,' upon receiving new birds at the Granja do Torto on May 9, 2026. He highlighted a Bahian rooster as plump, strong, and heat-resistant, with potential to reach up to 6 kg as an adult. The birds were delivered by breeder Mario Irineu Salviato of the Instituto Avis, including a pair of Sertaneja Balão chickens and a pair of Polish hens, with First Lady Janja Lula da Silva inviting the public to suggest names via social media.

item.title: Caiado diz que Moraes “ultrapassa limites institucionais”
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend the Dosimetry Law (Law 15.402/2026), stating that Moraes overstepped institutional limits by blocking a law approved by Congress. Caiado called the move judicial activism that attacks democracy, the separation of powers, and deepens polarization, diverting attention from issues like public security, education, and health.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que Brasil vai aposentar Lula
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) stated that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will be 'retired' by voters in 2026 and that the PT will lose political relevance starting in 2027. He made the remark during an event in Florianópolis, criticizing the current administration and claiming his government would not 'steal Lula's pension.' The senator also attended the launch of PL candidates for Senate and state government in Santa Catarina.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro volta a fazer dancinha em SC
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) performed his characteristic dance again at an event in Santa Catarina, where he launched the Senate candidacies of his brother Carlos Bolsonaro and deputy Carol De Toni. The act took place at Stage Music Park in Florianópolis, part of a strategy to soften the public image of the Bolsonaro family ahead of the 2026 elections. Similar performances were seen at PL candidate launches in Rondônia, Paraíba, and Rio Grande do Sul earlier this year.

item.title: Flávio se desdiz sobre reeleição e já fala em governo de '8 anos'
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro reversed his earlier stance, rejecting a constitutional amendment proposal he himself had introduced to end presidential re-election. While in Santa Catarina, he stated that if elected to the presidency, his term could last eight years, signaling support for re-election. This shift in position raises concerns about his political consistency regarding democratic term limits.

item.title: Ypê vira alvo de embate político nas redes sociais após suspensão da Anvisa
item.description: Cleaning products manufacturer Ypê became a target of social media debate after Anvisa suspended part of its production due to health safety concerns. The company, whose owner is identified as a supporter of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has become a symbol of what some call the 'Fla-Flu' of Brazilian politics, reflecting ideological polarization on social networks.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro lança irmão Carlos, ex-vereador do Rio, ao Senado por Santa Catarina
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president of Brazil, launched Carlos Bolsonaro, former Rio de Janeiro city councilor, as the PL's Senate pre-candidate for Santa Catarina at a political event on Saturday, November 9. The launch is part of the Bolsonarist group's strategy to expand its national presence ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: PT usa depoimento de criança para defender fim da 6 X 1
item.description: The PT shared a video featuring the emotional testimony of a child whose mother missed a school Mother’s Day event due to an exhausting 22-hour workday starting at 5 a.m. The post uses the account to advocate ending the 6×1 work schedule and to drive the debate on reducing working hours in Brazil, highlighting the Lula government’s bill (40 hours/week, 5×2 model) and ongoing constitutional amendments in Congress.

item.title: Lula usa acenos de Trump como estratégia para recuperar popularidade
item.description: Lula leveraged Donald Trump’s protectionist policies and sanctions against Brazil as an opportunity to strengthen internal government unity around defending national sovereignty and exports, adopting a stance of resistance to the U.S. that boosted his popularity. He also used personal meetings with Trump — at the UN General Assembly and the White House — to project himself as a respected global leader, contrasting his image with Bolsonaro’s and leveraging the relationship with the former U.S. president as an electoral asset to weaken the opposition.

item.title: Dados explicam por que, mesmo desgastado, Lula segue competitivo
item.description: Despite high rejection, Lula remains competitive in 2026 due to improved government approval since September 2025, with a 5.1-point drop in negative perception and a 7.4-point rise in positive ratings. This recovery was partly driven by the Trump tariff crisis on Brazilian goods, which allowed Lula to frame himself as a national defender and discomforted Bolsonarist right-wing sectors. The opposition, despite criticism, faces limits by assuming right-wing voters would automatically support any conservative candidate, overlooking electoral behavior complexity.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro: “Quatro anos é muito pouco para um mandato só”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro advocated for ending re-election but suggested a single term should last up to eight years, arguing four years is too short. The remarks were made at a political event in Florianópolis alongside PL allies, addressing business leaders.

item.title: Como Flávio Bolsonaro reagiu à decisão de Moraes de suspender dosimetria
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro, PL's pre-candidate for president, criticized Minister Alexandre de Moraes' decision to suspend the effects of the dosimetry law, calling it a "pen stroke" and suggesting a coordinated move, as Moraes had reportedly agreed with rapporteur Paulinho da Força's opinion. He accused the justice of undermining judicial credibility and argued that the monocratic decision contradicts the Congress-approved law backed by a majority.

item.title: Michelle adere a campanha nas redes e posta foto com detergente Ypê
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro posted an Instagram story showing Ypê detergent, aligning herself with a social media campaign supporting the brand after Anvisa suspended production of some of its products. The mobilization, initially driven by Bolsonaro supporters, claims the Lula government is using Anvisa to persecute the company, citing donations from the Beira family to Bolsonaro’s 2022 campaign. The movement has reversed from 2022, when boycotts were promoted, to now consumers defending Ypê on social media.

item.title: STF suspende julgamento de venda de terras de SP ao agro com desconto
item.description: The STF suspended for 90 days the judgment of the law allowing Tarcísio de Freitas’ government to sell public lands in São Paulo with discounts of up to 90% to farmers, following a request for review by Minister Gilmar Mendes. The action, filed by the PT, challenges the constitutionality of the State Land Regularization Program, a key agenda for the governor in favor of agribusiness. If another minister requests a review, the judgment will only resume after the 2026 elections.

item.title: Deputado bolsonarista manda ofício à CBF pedindo convocação de Neymar para Copa do Mundo
item.description: Bolsonarist deputy Hélio Lopes (PL-RJ) sent an official letter to the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) requesting Neymar's call-up for the 2026 World Cup, despite CBF being a private entity and selection being the coach's responsibility — currently held by Carlo Ancelotti. Lopes claims the request reflects the will of millions of Brazilians and portrays Neymar as a symbol of talent and hope. In the final year of his term, Lopes had 47 attendances, 20 unjustified absences, delivered no floor speeches, and served as rapporteur on no bills, having moved his electoral domicile to Roraima in a failed bid for a Senate seat backed by the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: Flávio tenta ocupar pauta de defesa das mulheres usada por Lula
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) sought to appeal to female voters at a PL event in Santa Catarina, addressing violence against women and citing Bolsonaro-era policies such as doubled emergency aid for single mothers and increased arrests of aggressors. He adopted the feminist violence agenda—a core theme of Lula’s government—to reduce his rejection among women, who make up 52.5% of the electorate, timed with Mother’s Day.
